[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John was baptized on 29 November 1702 in Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland to William Glasgow<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-XZ7 : 16 September 2021), William Glasgow in entry for John Glasgow, 1702.</ref>
== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1026]] is assessed at 92% (proved). The 1702 Kirknewton John entry explicitly names William, and father-1026 is the established account used for that local William household. Its composite 1682–1705 span lacks a residence or maternal bridge, leaving a modest identity reservation.

Record-defined father William is strong; identity across the 1682,1702,1705 entries is less secure. John’s possible later Meek household does not reduce this child link.

Next useful test: Compare original 1702 entry with 1682 and 1705 for residence and witnesses; reconcile 11 versus 29 November.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-XZ7 John, Kirknewton 1702: named father William; FamilySearch index]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Selected uncertain family — 16 October 2026 ===

Select William [[Glasgow-1026]] as the uncertain working father of John [[Glasgow-3481]], the combined Calder father account recorded in 1730 and with Christian Meek in 1751–1755. This adopts possible identity with John [[Glasgow-1544]], the child indexed at Kirknewton in 1702 with father William. The same name and parish and a normal adult generation favour this concrete child account over an unidentified origin: if baptised near birth in 1702, he would be about 28 in 1730 and 53 at the 1755 child. Those ages are conditional examples, not ages stated in the registers. The old circa 1710 birth was inferred from assumed age at the 1730 fatherhood and cannot exclude the 1702 child. The child’s existing father identity as William-1026 is itself qualified; no record explicitly identifies the later Meek husband as his son.

John-1544 and John-3481 remain separate profile accounts of a possible single man; the selection does not establish two distinct John sons. The 1702 date remains unreconciled: the child’s field uses a before 11 November boundary while its biography cites a 29 November baptism. Neither date is newly corrected. The later account combines the 1730 father of Jean, whose mother is omitted, with the 1751 and 1755 Meek household. That earlier adult identification remains a preferred working combination, not a continuous household proved by occupation, land or witnesses. John-81, estimated born 1709, remains a specific competing identity for the 1730 father. His Guthrie household is indexed with children in West Calder in 1751 and 1753 while the Meek household appears in Kirknewton in 1751 and Leith in 1755. That concrete overlap makes a simple succession of wives less persuasive; do not combine the full Guthrie and Meek families without resolving the entries. No birth estimate alone excludes John-81. Other local John origins remain possible. Ann McCook is not selected as John-3481’s mother: the reviewed 1702 child citation names William, and the attached Ann field does not supply an independently verified maternal clause. William’s existing uncertain John-3610 father and older family alternatives retain their grades; no date or family field is changed to force the new route.

This child’s dates, parent fields and unknown adult fate remain unchanged. The new adult father hypothesis is not a new son born in 1710 or proof of two John sons. === Possible John Glascow, Chester County land and committee ===
John Glascow is an adjoining landholder in a West-Nottingham Township, Chester County execution-sale notice for 22½ acres, late Michael Dintz’s estate, bounded by Abraham Bunting, John Glascow and others.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401494/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1773-04-28, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39401765/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1773-05-05, p.5].</ref>

John Glascow is appointed to provide for distressed families of Associators in actual service by the Chester County Committee of Inspection and Observation, in a resolution dated 13 August 1776.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/39398635/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1776-08-28, p.3].</ref>

The adjoining-owner and committee appointments may concern one man but do not name his parents or wife. They require an active adult in 1773 and 1776; the John who died in May 1769 cannot be that living participant.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1544]]. Could be an adult in 1776; no death or place evidence excludes him. No Pennsylvania connection.
